To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the catalytic asymmetric phase transfer reaction is a powerful tool for the synthesis of optically active amino acid derivatives and that aeruginosin analogs with a modified C-3 side chain showed potent serine protease inhibition activity.
we have developed a synthetic process for aeruginosin 298-A by catalytic asymmetric reactions and examined serine protease inhibition activities of aeruginosin and its analogs.
we developed an efficient and highly stereoselective synthetic route to aeruginosin and its analogs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a synthetic process for the preparation of a variety of aeruginosins and their analogs, and biological evaluation of their activities as serine protease inhibitors.
the development of an effective synthesis of aeruginosins and the elucidation of their structure-activity relationships.
the development of new methods for the synthesis of aeruginosins and analogs and the evaluation of their serine protease-inhibitory activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 1,2-diamine unit is crucial to the serine protease-inhibitory activity of aeruginosins.
the 4-hydroxymethyl group is important to the thrombin inhibitory activity of aeruginosins.
the 2,6-dimethylbenzoyl group is important for the inhibitory activity of serine proteases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3,3-dimethyl-2,3-dihydro-1H-pyrrol-2-yl group is essential for thrombin inhibitory activity.
the C-1, C-3, C-4, C-7, C-8, and C-11 stereocenters in aeruginosin were crucial for thrombin and trysin inhibition, while the C-2 and C-9 stereocenters had no effect.

the 5,5-disubstituted tetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one ring is a crucial part of the thrombin and tryspin inhibitory activity of aeruginosins, and that the stereochemistry of the C3 and C6 hydroxyls of the tetrahydro-3H-pyrrol-3-one ring is also important for the inhibitory activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the introduction of a methyl group at the C-3 position is essential for the inhibitory activity.
the introduction of a hydroxyl group at C(2) and C(5) of aeruginosins 298-A and 98-A is crucial for inhibitory activity against serine proteases.

a 2,3- trans -3-hydroxy-4-methoxy-2-methylproline moiety is essential for the activity, and the 2,3-trans -4,5-cis -4,5- trans -3-amino-4-hydroxy-2-methylpyrrolidine moiety is also essential for the inhibitory activity against trypsin.
